prompt: You are the test author this time: write isCorrect so it accepts a correct MaxFinder and rejects broken ones. Note that the method is generic, so your checker can try it with more than one kind of element. Complete the checker in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Two traps here are about the inputs you choose rather than the code you read. A list that happens to start with its largest element cannot tell "finds the maximum" apart from "returns the first element", so the order of your test data is itself part of the test. And a list of all-negative numbers is the only thing that catches an implementation seeded with 0 instead of with the first element -- with [3, 9, 4] it looks perfect. Because the method is generic, a checker that only ever passes Integers leaves the compareTo contract half-tested; a list of Strings costs one extra line and covers the other half.
hints: Use a list whose FIRST element is not the answer, and then a list where it is: [3, 9, 4] and [9, 3, 4] together separate 'finds the max' from 'returns the first'.
Try an all-negative list such as [-5, -1, -3] -> -1. An implementation that starts its search at 0 passes every positive test and fails this one.
The method is generic: pass a List<String> as well as a List<Integer>, and remember the empty list must give back null rather than throwing.
